syncApiUrlsToInstanceUrl.label: Sync API URLs to instance URL
syncApiUrlsToInstanceUrl.description: Rewrite URLs returned by Forgejo (html_url, avatar_url, download_url, etc.) to use the configured instance URL. Turn off if you want to keep the server-declared addresses.

declaredServerVersion.label: Server version
declaredServerVersion.description: Declare this instance's Forgejo version for when the automatic probe cannot read /api/v1/version — a reverse proxy or path prefix that blocks it, an unrecognised fork, a timeout. {version} is accepted, and so is that version with a build suffix such as +gitea-…. Leave empty to use the probe. A declared version always wins over the probe and decides which features are offered.

instanceEditor.backToListTitle: Leave this editor and return to the instance list

debug.title: Debug Logging
debug.description: Enable request/response logging to the Forgejo Toolkit output channel.

notifications.title: Notifications
notifications.description: How this window watches your instances for unread notifications.
notifications.enabledDefault: Default on: polling works as soon as an instance is configured.
notifications.disabledHint: While this is off the unread badge and the alerts stop updating.

multiWindow.title: Multiple windows
multiWindow.lease: Poll and alert from one window only
multiWindow.default: Default on: one window polls and raises the alerts, the others stay quiet.
multiWindow.description: The lease tries to follow the window you are working in. Where VS Code's focus state cannot be trusted, the current holder keeps it, so the alerts stay with one window and none is lost — this is the state the extension reports when it cannot decide.
multiWindow.offHint: With this off every window polls and alerts on its own, which uses more requests.

mcp.title: MCP Server
mcp.description: Expose your Forgejo instances to agents in agent mode, as MCP servers.
mcp.enabledDefault: Default on: the servers work as soon as an instance is configured.
mcp.disabledHint: Turning this off withdraws the server definitions immediately and stops the workspace-repository mapping and the local broker; a client that is already connected keeps the server process it started until you reload the window.

writeTools.title: Write tools
writeTools.description: Off by default, one switch per tool. While one is on, an agent acts under your account: VS Code asks you to confirm each call, but you can turn that confirmation off for a tool, and a client other than VS Code may not ask at all.
writeTools.default: Default off: every write tool stays off until you turn on the one you mean.
writeTools.createIssueComment: Create issue and pull request comments

audit.title: Audit
audit.enabled: Also write the audit to a file
audit.default: Default off: the audit stays in the Forgejo Toolkit output channel, and is lost when the window closes.
audit.file: When this is on, each record is also appended to `mcp-write-audit.jsonl` in the extension's log folder (VS Code: "Developer: Open Logs Folder"), on top of the output channel. The file is capped at 1 MB with two rolled files.

ai.title: AI
ai.description: The whole AI area's own switch, above every AI feature's own switch.
ai.enabledDefault: Default on: this switch is the layer above the feature switches, so leaving it on enables nothing by itself.
ai.disabledHint: AI is off, so no AI feature runs and no model is asked for anything — neither this editor's chat models nor a configured endpoint — and nothing is sent to one. Everything below stays visible and editable while it is off: turning this switch back on needs no reconfiguration.

aiPreReview.title: AI Pre-Review
aiPreReview.description: A chat model reads a pull request and proposes line-level review comments; you pick the ones you agree with, and only those are written as drafts of a pending review. The extension never submits a review.
aiPreReview.enabledDefault: Default off: nothing is sent to a model until you turn this on.
aiPreReview.disabledHint: The prompt scope and the model below are configuration; a run uses them only while this is on.
aiPreReview.scopeDescription: What the prompt may carry. This is the only place the answer is recorded: every run reads it from here, and `ask` means the question has not been answered yet.
aiPreReview.scopeDefault: Default: `ask` — the first run asks once and writes your answer here.

scopeOption.ask: Ask before each run — nothing is requested, sent or written until you answer
scopeOption.metadata-only: Metadata only — no code: the title, the branch names, the changed-file paths with their line counts, and review-comment metadata
scopeOption.changed-lines-only: Changed lines only — the added and removed lines with their file and hunk headers, and no unchanged context
scopeOption.full-diff: Full diff — every hunk, including the unchanged context lines, but not the files' own text
scopeOption.changed-files: Changed files — the whole diff plus the full text of every changed file at the pull request's head version

prDescription.title: AI: Pull Request Description
prDescription.description: A chat model drafts a description from the comparison the create-pull-request form is about to submit, and fills it into the description field as an editable draft. You still create the pull request yourself, and a draft that could not be produced leaves the field as you wrote it.
prDescription.enabled: Offer "Generate description" on the create-pull-request form
prDescription.enabledDefault: Default off: nothing is read or sent until you turn this on.
prDescription.disabledHint: The prompt scope below is configuration; a draft uses it only while this is on.
prDescription.scopeDescription: What the draft's prompt may carry. This is the only place the answer is recorded: every draft reads it from here, and `ask` means the question has not been answered yet.
prDescription.scopeDefault: Default: `ask` — the first draft asks once and writes your answer here.

scopeOption.ask: Ask before each draft — nothing is requested, sent or written until you answer
scopeOption.commits-only: Commits and changed-file list — the branch names, the commits with their subjects, bodies, authors and dates, and the path and status of every changed file, with no file content
scopeOption.commits-and-files: Commits, changed files and their text — the same plus the full text of the changed files at the head branch

aiPreReviewModel.description: Which chat model reviews a pull request. VS Code only lists the models at run time, so this dropdown is loaded from the running extension.
aiPreReviewModel.optionDescription: The brief goes to the "{vendor}" provider. maxInputTokens={tokens}
aiPreReviewModel.notStorable: This model has no vendor/name form for the setting to store.
aiPreReviewModel.configuredNotOffered: The setting currently holds "{value}", which is not one of the models offered here. A pre-review run refuses until it names one.
aiPreReviewModel.loading: Loading the models VS Code offers...
aiPreReviewModel.saved: Saved: {value}. Every pre-review run uses this model until you change it.
aiPreReviewModel.cleared: Cleared. The next pre-review run asks which model to use.
aiPreReviewModel.note: The choice is stored in the setting forgejoToolkit.aiPreReviewModel, which you can also edit by hand in VS Code's Settings, or change with the command forgejoToolkit.aiPreReviewChooseModel.

aiProviders.title: AI Endpoints
aiProviders.description: OpenAI-compatible endpoints this extension may send to. The address, the model list and the header names are configuration; the API key and every header value are stored in the editor's secret storage and are never written into settings.
aiProviders.backToListTitle: Leave this editor and return to the endpoint list

row.insecure: Plain http:// — the request and the answer are not encrypted in transit.
row.shadowed: Not sent: the authentication style already owns {names}.
row.noModels: No model is declared for this endpoint.

rejected.title: Entries that could not be read
rejected.intro: These entries in forgejoToolkit.aiProviders were refused rather than guessed at. Nothing is sent to them, and editing an endpoint here leaves them in place.

testReport.notRunTitle: The endpoint "{name}" was not tested: nothing was sent.
testReport.sourceAutomatic: From the automatic model-list probe this page ran after the address, the authentication style or the credential changed.
testReport.sourceExplicit: From the Test connection button you pressed.
testReport.shadowed: Not sent: the authentication style already owns {names}.

policy.transportAuto: auto — this editor's models first, then the configured default below
policy.transportOpenAiCompatible: openai-compatible — the configured default below only
policy.transportDescription: Which route an AI feature takes when its own per-feature override (further down) says nothing.
policy.precedenceAuto: auto prefers this editor's model when one is available, and uses the configured endpoint when it is not.
policy.precedenceEditor: vscode-lm uses this editor's chat model only. Its list is in the AI pre-review section above; the endpoint surface below is hidden while this is selected.
policy.hiddenForEditor: The endpoint surface — the configured endpoints, the default endpoint and model, and the policy gates below — is hidden while the transport is vscode-lm, because nothing here would be used. Choose auto or openai-compatible to see it again.
policy.precedenceEndpoint: openai-compatible uses the configured endpoint only. Nothing here asks this editor's models, so their row is hidden above; choose auto or vscode-lm to see it again.
policy.timeoutDescription: How long an endpoint may send nothing before the request is aborted (1000–600000). This is an idle window rather than a total limit, so a long answer that keeps arriving survives; a second, wider limit of ten times this value bounds the whole request.

defaultModel.modelPlaceholder: The model name the endpoint expects
defaultModel.description: Every AI feature without an override of its own uses this endpoint and model. It is what the transport above means by "the configured endpoint", and with no default the direct route has nothing to send to.
defaultModel.statusUnset: No default endpoint is configured yet. Until one is, the direct route uses a single configured endpoint only when exactly one is configured and it declares a model; give the default a value to be explicit. To pick one here, the endpoint has to be configured above first.
defaultModel.saved: The default endpoint and model were saved.
defaultModel.cleared: The default endpoint and model were removed.
defaultModel.halfConfigured: The default needs both halves: an endpoint and the model to ask it for. A model on its own names nowhere to send to, and no model is guessed for an endpoint.
defaultModel.missingProvider: The default names the endpoint "{id}", which is not configured. A run refuses until it is fixed or the default is removed.

bindings.title: Per-Feature Overrides
bindings.description: An override is optional: it exists for the feature that needs a stronger or more private model than the default. Every feature without one follows the default endpoint and model above.
bindings.none: Do not override — follow the default above
bindings.modelPlaceholder: The model name the endpoint expects
bindings.empty: No AI feature in this build can be overridden.
bindings.missingProvider: This override names the endpoint "{id}", which is not configured. A pre-review refuses until it is fixed or the override is removed.

notUsable.title: No AI model is available
notUsable.installRoute: Install an extension that contributes a chat model and sign in to it. The language model API lists the models every such extension contributes, not only one vendor's — a signed-out editor and a fork with no model provider look the same here.
notUsable.endpointRoute: Configure an OpenAI-compatible endpoint: its address, the models it has, a key, and one connection test. On an editor with no model provider at all, this is the only route.
notUsable.bindHint: Nothing says which endpoint serves this feature: bind it under Feature Bindings, or leave the transport on "auto" with exactly one endpoint configured.

status.removed: The endpoint "{id}" was removed, along with the secrets stored for it.
status.secretSaved: The value was stored in the editor's secret storage.
status.loadFailed: The AI endpoint settings could not be read: {error}
status.notFound: This endpoint is no longer configured.

editor.idDescription: Letters, digits, "_" and "-" only. The id is part of the key each stored secret uses, which is why it is fixed once the endpoint exists.
editor.idLocked: The id cannot be changed: the stored secrets are keyed by it.
editor.idCreateWarning: Decide the id now: it cannot be changed once the endpoint is saved. Every stored key and header value is filed under it, so changing it later would mean losing them.
editor.name: Display name
editor.nameDescription: What the consent question, the log and this page call the endpoint.
editor.baseUrlDescription: Used exactly as written apart from a trailing slash: /v1 is deliberately not appended, because Azure's address and a gateway's /openai/v1 would both be made wrong by it. Only /chat/completions and /models are appended.
editor.authBearer: bearer — send the key as an Authorization: Bearer header
editor.authApiKeyHeader: api-key-header — send the key as an api-key header (Azure)
editor.authNone: none — send no credential (a local server)
editor.modelsDescription: A declaration, not a whitelist: it fills in the chooser and is what a feature binding can name, while a model id typed by hand is still accepted. An empty list is not a failure.
editor.modelDuplicate: This model id is already declared above.
editor.headersDescription: Only the names are configuration. Every value is stored in the editor's secret storage, and api-version travels as a query parameter rather than as a header.
editor.headerDuplicate: This header name is already declared above.
editor.headerSet: A value is stored. Leave this empty to keep it.
editor.headerShadowed: The authentication style above sends this header itself, so this declared name is not sent.
editor.headerQueryCarried: Sent as a query parameter rather than as a header.
editor.keyDescription: Stored in the editor's secret storage, never in settings. Leave the field empty to keep whatever is stored.
editor.keySet: A key is stored. Leave the field empty to keep it.
editor.keyNotNeeded: This endpoint sends no credential, so there is no key to store.
editor.secretFailed: The endpoint was saved, but a stored value could not be written: {error}

probe.added: Added {count} model(s) from the endpoint's /models; they are ordinary rows you can edit or remove.
probe.unchanged: The endpoint's /models reported no model this list does not already declare.
probe.failed: The probe did not get an answer: the endpoint's own reason is in the report below.
probe.refused: The probe sent nothing: the reason is in the report below.
probe.notConsent: This does not mean requests are allowed. The probe only read the model list; the global AI switch and each feature's own consent question are what decide whether content is ever sent.

status.permissionSaved: Instance saved, but the token is missing the {permission} scope, so the dashboard cannot list your repositories: {message}
status.probeFailed: Instance saved, but the dashboard could not list your repositories: {message}

importPreview.title: Import Preview
importPreview.error: Could not read the import file: {message}
importPreview.dropped: {count} entry(ies) in this file could not be used and were skipped.

ai.title: AI endpoints in this file
ai.policyNote: Importing stores these endpoints as configuration only. It does not turn AI on and it does not turn any AI feature on: those are switches only you can set, and a feature still asks what may leave your machine before it sends anything.
ai.secretsIncluded: This encrypted file carries the credentials for its {count} endpoint(s), and they will be stored in the editor's secret storage, not in settings.
ai.noSecrets: This file was not encrypted, so it carries no API key and no header value for its {count} endpoint(s). Import them as configuration; add each credential afterwards in the AI endpoints settings, or no request to them can be authenticated.
ai.insecure: {count} of these addresses is plain http://, so the request and the answer would not be encrypted in transit.
ai.rename: Import alongside it under a new id
ai.bindings: {count} feature binding(s) in this file will be applied for the endpoints it imports.

aiPreReview.title: AI pre-review: review the proposed comments
aiPreReview.coverage: This run covered the whole pull request: {count} changed file(s).
aiPreReview.coveragePartial: This run covered {count} of the pull request's {total} changed files.
aiPreReview.selectHint: Check the comments you agree with. Nothing is checked by default, and only the checked ones are created — as drafts of a pending review, which this extension never submits.
aiPreReview.restoreBody: Restore the wording the model proposed
aiPreReview.bodyEmpty: This body is empty, so nothing can be created from it. Write something, or restore the wording the model proposed.
aiPreReview.bodyLimitReached: This body has reached the {limit}-character limit for one comment. Nothing is cut for you: shorten it before adding more.
aiPreReview.bodyOverLimit: This body is {count} characters, over the {limit}-character limit for one comment. Shorten it, or restore the wording the model proposed.
aiPreReview.blockedHint: A checked comment cannot be created as it stands — see the message on its card.
aiPreReview.openDiff: Open the diff at this line
aiPreReview.bodyTruncated: This body was cut to the extension's per-comment limit.
aiPreReview.empty: The model proposed no comment that passed the anchor validation, so there is nothing to confirm.
aiPreReview.nothingSelected: Nothing is created until you check a comment and press Create.
aiPreReview.resultCreated: Created {count} draft comment(s) in the pending review. Read them before you submit the review — this extension never submits it.
aiPreReview.resultPartial: Created {count} draft comment(s); the rest failed: {failure}
aiPreReview.resultFailed: No draft comment could be created: {failure}
